title: Microcredit Surge experiment and enterprise SQ playbook
creator: Evan Chu
description: Run a staged experiment that tests a lightweight, time-limited microcredit model (small, periodic top-ups + surge credits) aimed at maximizing new-account activation and early retention while simultaneously producing a reusable security questionnaire (SQ) runbook for enterprise conversions. This ticket covers design, metric definitions, engineering gates, and a short SQ playbook to accelerate sales/legal exchanges for high-value trials.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment deployed to 10% of new signups for 4 weeks with telemetry; no client-visible billing regressions
Primary metric lift: +8% 14-day active usage (DAU) for experiment cohort vs control, with equal or better cost-per-activation
Defined surge-signal rules and thresholds implemented as feature flags and shown in the analytics dashboard
Enterprise SQ playbook drafted and reviewed by Legal & Security, with owner and template ready for reuse
Rollout guardrails documented: max free monthly credit consumption, abuse detection signals, and fallback behavior
experiment_matrix: Variant A: Baseline (current 500 free credits one-shot, 14-day expiry)
Variant B: Microcredits (5 top-ups of 150 credits each, first top-up immediate, remaining every 7 days), 30-day shelfing
Variant C: Micro + Surge (same microcredits + event-triggered surge 500 credits on first high-utility call), 30-day expiry
Variant D: Decay model (1000 credits upfront but daily decay of 5% after day 7), test for shortened commitment
analytics_goals: Primary: 14-day activation rate (first 3 high-value calls) delta vs control
Safety: percent of accounts hitting abuse heuristics, average tokens consumed per new account
Enterprise signal: number of qualified SQLs originating from accounts that received surge credit
rollout_plan: Week 0: Feature-flagged backend changes + small schema for credit buckets (ENG-2321)
Week 1: Internal dogfood and QA; smoke tests for billing & expiry; deploy analytics events
Week 2-5: 4-week experiment window, 10% traffic split, weekly checks on abuse & cost
Week 6: Analyze cohorts, review with Growth/Finance/Sales; decide on further rollouts or modified variant
Post-analysis: if positive, staged ramp and productization with console controls for administrators
engineering_dependencies: ENG-3410 - analytics-pipeline: new events for surge and velocity
ENG-3650 - abuse-detection: throttles and alerts for free-tier misuse
